answer: For standard reimbursement claims, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2], whereas under Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. Additionally, the sources note a conflict with an archived 2024 guideline, which previously stated the deadline was 15 days from discharge [3].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans, unless explicitly waived in writing on the policy schedule by Aurora [3][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the pre-existing disease waiting period is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].

Across all plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, under the Aurora Gold plan, air ambulance is covered up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or within 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation during this period, the premium is refunded minus proportionate risk premium for the cover period, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].

No, everything will not be paid [1][5]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured (₹10,000 per day) [1][2]. Because the room cost of ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, an eligibility ratio of 0.667 is applied, leading to proportionate deductions across multiple billed expenses [1][5].

Dependent parents can be covered under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but not under the Bronze plan [1]. Adding a parent changes how the premium is calculated, as it is determined by the age of the eldest member covered; this often makes adding them to a floater more expensive than buying an individual senior-citizen policy, and advisers must present both options in writing [4].

To continue your baby's cover beyond the initial 90 days, you must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add the newborn as a dependent with guaranteed-issue cover and no medical underwriting [1]. Additionally, if you are filing a reimbursement claim for the delivery or hospitalisation, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [3].
